I don't think the guy that has the top comment knows what maintenance weight means. If you gain weight while you are supposedly on your maintenance calorie intake, then that isn't your maintenance calorie in.

I think what he was saying is that the calculations (such as on an online TDEE calculator) for maintenance caloric intake are for people without these conditions. Since the TDEE is somewhat reduced with these conditions, a person eating what they think their TDEE should be (by using the online calculator) is actually eating over maintenance, thus gaining weight. What a lot of people don't get is that those calculations are just estimates, and that you have to adjust your calorie intake to fit your individual needs (such as if you have a condition that reduces your TDEE).

The answer underneath it does explain a bit about how the weight gain is per year. If you don't understand that your caloric intake need to be a lot lower, you'll probably continually over eat at the 'correct' level, and be baffled why weight loss doesn't happen at 1500 cals, and you even seem to gain a bit at that level. This happened with me for years. Dr insisted I was not weighing portions or was forgetting that I'd eaten stuff.

BMR for IR women with PCOS is about 700 lower than normal. Which means fast weight gain on a 1500 calorie diet is pretty easy (1/2 lb week at a normal body weight). If you've been told you need 1800 to 2000 to maintain.. well, you'll get fat fast even though you aren't 'over eating'. PCOS women will gain weight at a calorie intake that would normally cause weight loss in a metabolically normal person. It's certainly not a 'junk food and non-stop soda' diet calorie level, it's healthy food in moderate portion sizes causing weight gain.

The lower BMR was not mentioned to me once in all the years I went to the doctors about my PCOS, found out here, of all places. I've asked around a lot of other PCOS sufferers, none of them knew this either. People who need to know this aren't being informed.

I figured out years ago the only way I was going to shift it was if I went under 1,000 calories a day, or keto (which is way less painful). I currently deal with my low BMR by sticking to a low carb diet and walking everywhere.
